subject: Read the taskq queue from disk so the panel shows what the transcript cannot
description:
The task panel reconstructs taskq tasks from the transcript alone: the id from the record, the description from the command line. Both halves can be missing in practice. A description built in a shell variable is unrecoverable (v1.119.0 makes that honest by recording nothing rather than the literal dollar-D), a heredoc or command substitution is gone entirely, and a record read past a resume point has no create at all.

But the queue is a FILE STORE, and the truth is sitting on disk: tasks/*.json at the git root of the session cwd, with the full subject, description, status, owner and blockers.

engine/tasks.rs already has the pattern -- see the merge doc comment: "Merge the live on-disk state over the op-log reconstruction: disk wins per task id (it is the queue current truth and carries full detail); op-log items fill in for pruned/gc-d files." That is written for the harness own task sidecar. Point the same mechanism at the taskq store and every gap above closes at once.

Sketch: resolve the session cwd to a git root, read tasks/*.json there (task_from_json is already on the seam), merge over the op-log list with disk winning per id. Guard it: a session whose cwd no longer exists, a repo whose queue belongs to different work, and the cost of stat-ing a directory on every fold.

NOTE for whoever picks this up: pass --description as a LITERAL, never as a shell variable. The viewer reads the command line, so "$D" records nothing. This very task was first filed that way, which is a fair demonstration of the bug it describes.

Definition of done: a session that ran taskq shows every task with its real description regardless of how the command was written; a session with no queue is unchanged; the byte-identical gate re-baselined for the panel rows that gain text.
activeForm: Merging the taskq store into the task panel
outcome:
Added engine::taskq::queue_tasks (reads tasks/*.json AND tasks/archive/*.json at the git root, honouring GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES so test scratch under target/ sees no repo) and engine::tasks::enrich_from_queue, wired through one new facade discover::session_task_view that replaced all four tasks::merged call sites. ENRICH-ONLY, not merged() semantics: a taskq queue is repo-scoped, so letting it add rows would show every session the whole team queue and letting it win would let one queue text overwrite another on a bare numeric-id collision. The subject is the discriminator (exact, or prefix-matched through the record 120-char truncation); an empty-subject #125 stub is never enriched. Costs nothing when nothing needs filling: the queue is not looked for unless some task lacks text.

Fixing it surfaced a real decoder bug and that is fixed here too: shell_words is not a shell, and an ODD apostrophe in a heredoc body (a task description saying "Cursor d") flipped its quote state and hid the next create boundary, so one draft was recovered where two were written -- it paired with the FIRST record, putting task #10 text under #9 and dropping #10 and #13 entirely. Now unclosed quoting yields NO drafts, and a create record stands its task up on its own before any draft resolves onto it, so a lost draft costs a description rather than a row.

Measured on this session: 13 of 15 repo tasks now match disk exactly with full descriptions (was 8 mis-titled or empty); #10 and #13 are back. FOLD_VERSION 20 -> 21. Byte gate PASS with no re-baseline. Ships in v1.120.0.

log.msg: Honest limit for the reported session: /Users/hong/code/agent-metrics has an EMPTY queue (tasks/ holds only archive/ and README.md), so queue_tasks returns None and enrichment does nothing there. Its two blank rows are #1, migrated to the user queue so its repo file is gone, and #12, the phantom from taskq-DESIGN.md filed as #16. Repo-tier only by design: a u-prefixed id would need the user store at $TASKQ_HOME, and pre-rev-4 records carry no tier, so the id alone cannot be routed.
